Attribute Commands.name: DeleteAndReplaceAttributes
Attribute Commands.description: Deletes fills, line types, surfaces or building materials and replaces each by another attribute of the same type wherever it was used, like Delete and Replace in the Attribute Manager. Every reference is rewritten to the replacement, the way ReindexAttributes rewrites them: the fields of the elements in the floor plan and in every view and layout, the parameters of library part based elements, their memo data, the tool defaults, the Favorites, the other attributes that refer to it (composites, building materials, surfaces, profiles, MEP systems) and the graphic override rules. Elements on a hidden or locked layer are changed too: their layers are shown and unlocked for the change and put back afterwards (in the current window). If an element cannot be changed (it is locked itself, or not reserved in Teamwork), everything is put back and that attribute is not deleted. Elements from hotlinked modules cannot be changed and are listed. Indices typed into GDL scripts are not found, and the frame and panel classes of curtain wall Favorites and of the Curtain Wall tool default keep the deleted attribute (named in the warnings). If a tool default, Favorite, attribute or rule cannot be rewritten to the replacement, it keeps a copy of the deleted attribute with its name and a new attribute id, named in the warnings. The whole call is one undo step. With dryRun true nothing is changed and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each attribute that passes the checks gets wouldDelete and lists every reference a real run would rewrite (elements, tool defaults, Favorites, other attributes, graphic override rules, elements from hotlinked modules). Available from Archicad 27.

    attribute of the same type wherever it was used, like Delete and Replace in the
    Attribute Manager. Every reference is rewritten to the replacement, the way
    ReindexAttributes rewrites them: the fields of the elements in the floor plan and in
    every view and layout, the parameters of library part based elements, their memo data,
    the tool defaults, the Favorites, the other attributes that refer to it (composites,
    building materials, surfaces, profiles, MEP systems) and the graphic override rules.
    Elements on a hidden or locked layer are changed too: their layers are shown and
    unlocked for the change and put back afterwards (in the current window). If an element
    cannot be changed (it is locked itself, or not reserved in Teamwork), everything is put
    back and that attribute is not deleted. Elements from hotlinked modules cannot be
    changed and are listed. Indices typed into GDL scripts are not found, and the frame and
    panel classes of curtain wall Favorites and of the Curtain Wall tool default keep the
    deleted attribute (named in the warnings). If a tool default, Favorite, attribute or
    rule cannot be rewritten to the replacement, it keeps a copy of the deleted attribute
    with its name and a new attribute id, named in the warnings. The whole call is one undo
    step. With dryRun true nothing is changed and no undo step is created: the response has
    dryRun set to true, and each attribute that passes the checks gets wouldDelete and lists

Attribute Commands.name: GetMissingAttributes
Attribute Commands.description: Lists the references of placed elements to layers, fills, surfaces, building materials, composites, profiles, line types, pen tables and zone categories that do not exist in the project, for the given types or all of them, and of the tool defaults, Favorites, graphic override rules, Model View Options combinations and attributes: the structured counterpart of the missing attributes report of Archicad's GDL palette. Every element of the floor plan and of every view and layout (hotlinked ones too) is checked, and so is every tool default and Favorite (with its sub-elements): its layer, its attribute fields and memo data as ReindexAttributes finds them, its composite or profile when its structure type uses one, a drawing's own pen table, and its library part parameters of attribute types; of every graphic override rule the line type, fill and surface it overrides with; of every Model View Options combination the surfaces and line types of the stair and railing schemes and the library part settings' GDL parameters of attribute types; of every composite the building materials of its skins and the line types of its separators, of every building material its cut fill and cut surface, of every surface the fill of its vectorial hatching, of every MEP system its fill, center line type and surfaces, and of every profile the building material, surface or fill of each skin and its contour, cut end and edge line types. The sources input limits the check to elements, tool defaults, Favorites, graphic override rules, Model View Options or attributes. Attribute Commands.name: ImportAttributesFromProject
Attribute Commands.description: Imports Line, Fill, ZoneCategory, PenTable, OperationProfile, Composite, Profile and LayerCombination attributes from another project or template file into the open project, with their complete definition (symbol and percent fills included), like Append or Overwrite by name in Archicad's Attribute Manager. The lines and fills a composite or profile uses are matched by name; its building materials and surfaces, and the layers of a layer combination, keep their index only with referencesByIndex, since Archicad does not read these types from a closed file. An attribute with a reference that cannot be mapped is not imported. A new attribute gets a new guid: Archicad does not hand out the guids stored in the source file. An attribute whose name already exists is skipped, or overwritten in place with overwriteExisting. dryRun reports what would happen without changing anything. The names are the legacy 8-bit names of the source file. Available from Archicad 27.
Attribute Commands.method_code:
def import_attributes_from_project(
    self,
    project_file_path: str,
    attribute_types: list[AttributeType],
    attribute_names: None | list[str] = None,
    overwrite_existing: None | bool = None,
    dry_run: None | bool = None,
    references_by_index: None | bool = None
) -> ErrorItem | ImportedAttributesByType:
    """
    Imports Line, Fill, ZoneCategory, PenTable, OperationProfile, Composite, Profile and
    LayerCombination attributes from another project or template file into the open project,
    with their complete definition (symbol and percent fills included), like Append or
    Overwrite by name in Archicad's Attribute Manager. The lines and fills a composite or
    profile uses are matched by name; its building materials and surfaces, and the layers of
    a layer combination, keep their index only with referencesByIndex, since Archicad does
    not read these types from a closed file. An attribute with a reference that cannot be
    mapped is not imported. A new attribute gets a new guid: Archicad does not hand out the
    guids stored in the source file. An attribute whose name already exists is skipped, or
    overwritten in place with overwriteExisting. dryRun reports what would happen without
    changing anything. The names are the legacy 8-bit names of the source file. Available
    from Archicad 27.

    Args:
        project_file_path (str): The absolute path of the project or template file (for
            example .pln or .tpl) to import the attributes from.
        attribute_types (list[AttributeType]): The attribute types to import, in this order.
            Line, Fill, ZoneCategory, PenTable, OperationProfile, Composite, Profile and
            LayerCombination can be imported. Layer, Surface, BuildingMaterial and MEPSystem
            fail with an error item: Archicad does not read them from a closed file. A
            Composite, Profile or LayerCombination refers to other attributes, see
            referencesByIndex; list Line and Fill before them to import the lines and fills
            they use.
        attribute_names (None | list[str]): Import only the attributes with these names. All
            attributes of the given types are imported when it is omitted.
        overwrite_existing (None | bool): What happens to an attribute whose name already
            exists in the open project. false (default): it is skipped and the existing
            attribute is kept. true: the existing attribute is overwritten with the imported
            definition and keeps its index and guid.
        dry_run (None | bool): If true, nothing is changed: the response reports what an
            import would do.
        references_by_index (None | bool): How the BuildingMaterial, Surface and Layer
            references of an imported Composite, Profile or LayerCombination are mapped.
            Archicad does not read these attributes from a closed file, so their names are
            unknown and they cannot be matched by name. false (default): an attribute with
            such a reference is not imported (result failed). true: the reference keeps its
            index and refers to the attribute with that index in the open project, which is
            right only when both files share these attributes at the same indexes, for
            example because they come from the same template. Line and Fill references are
            always matched by name.

    Returns:
        ErrorItem | ImportedAttributesByType

    Raises:
        ArchicadAPIError: If the API returns an error response.
        RequestError: If there is a network or connection error.
        pydantic.ValidationError: If the parameters, or the API Response fail validation.
    """
    params_dict = {
            'projectFilePath': project_file_path,
            'attributeTypes': attribute_types,
            'attributeNames': attribute_names,
            'overwriteExisting': overwrite_existing,
            'dryRun': dry_run,
            'referencesByIndex': references_by_index,
        }
    validated_params = ImportAttributesFromProjectParameters(**params_dict)
    response_dict = self._core.post_tapir_command(
        "ImportAttributesFromProject",
        validated_params.model_dump(mode='json', by_alias=True, exclude_none=True)
    )
    validated_response = TypeAdapter(ImportAttributesFromProjectResult).validate_python(response_dict)
    return validated_response

Attribute Commands.name: ReindexAttributes
Attribute Commands.description: Moves fills, line types, surfaces, building materials and zone categories to new indices, the way ReindexLayers moves layers. Archicad cannot renumber an attribute, so the attribute is recreated at its new index (free indices below it are filled with temporary attributes, which are deleted again) and every reference to the old index is rewritten to the new one: the fields of the elements in the floor plan and in every view and layout, the parameters of library part based elements, the memo data of roofs, slabs, meshes, morphs, curtain walls, beams, columns, stairs and interior elevations, the tool defaults, the Favorites (with their sub-elements: a curtain wall's frame and panel classes, a stair's structures), the other attributes that refer to it (composites, building materials, surfaces, profiles, MEP systems) and the graphic override rules. Only then is the old attribute deleted. The new attribute has a new attribute id (Archicad does not keep a given id); its name, definition and attribute folder are the old ones. Elements on a hidden or locked layer cannot be changed, so their layers are shown and unlocked for the move and put back afterwards (in the current window, as Archicad keeps these flags per window). If an element still cannot be changed (it is locked itself, or not reserved in Teamwork), everything is put back and that attribute is not moved. Elements from hotlinked modules cannot be changed and are listed; their module file has to be reindexed on its own. Indices typed into GDL scripts are not found, and the frame and panel classes of curtain wall Favorites and of the Curtain Wall tool default keep the old index (Archicad does not take them from ACAPI_Favorite_Change, so such Favorites are left as they are and named in the warnings). dryRun lists every reference without changing anything.     indices, the way ReindexLayers moves layers. Archicad cannot renumber an attribute, so
    the attribute is recreated at its new index (free indices below it are filled with
    temporary attributes, which are deleted again) and every reference to the old index is
    rewritten to the new one: the fields of the elements in the floor plan and in every view
    and layout, the parameters of library part based elements, the memo data of roofs,
    slabs, meshes, morphs, curtain walls, beams, columns, stairs and interior elevations,
    the tool defaults, the Favorites (with their sub-elements: a curtain wall's frame and
    panel classes, a stair's structures), the other attributes that refer to it (composites,
    building materials, surfaces, profiles, MEP systems) and the graphic override rules.
    Only then is the old attribute deleted. The new attribute has a new attribute id
    (Archicad does not keep a given id); its name, definition and attribute folder are the
    old ones. Elements on a hidden or locked layer cannot be changed, so their layers are
    shown and unlocked for the move and put back afterwards (in the current window, as
    Archicad keeps these flags per window). If an element still cannot be changed (it is
    locked itself, or not reserved in Teamwork), everything is put back and that attribute
    is not moved. Elements from hotlinked modules cannot be changed and are listed; their
    module file has to be reindexed on its own. Indices typed into GDL scripts are not
    found, and the frame and panel classes of curtain wall Favorites and of the Curtain Wall
    tool default keep the old index (Archicad does not take them from ACAPI_Favorite_Change,
    so such Favorites are left as they are and named in the warnings). dryRun lists every
    reference without changing anything. The whole call is one undo step. Pens, layers (see
    ReindexLayers) and the other attribute types are not supported. Available from Archicad
    27.

    Args:
        attribute_type (ReindexableAttributeType)
        attributes (list[AttributeReindexData]): The attributes to move to a new index,

Attribute Commands.name: ReindexLayers
Attribute Commands.description: Moves layers to new indices. Archicad cannot renumber an attribute, so each layer is recreated at its new index (free indices below it are filled with temporary layers, which are deleted again), gets the old layer's state in every layer combination, and then every element of the old layer is moved to it, in the floor plan and in every view and layout database, with the tool defaults on that layer. Only when the old layer is empty everywhere is it deleted, and the new layer gets its name, flags and folder. If an element cannot be moved (it is locked, not reserved in Teamwork, or comes from a hotlinked module), that layer is left as it was. The new layer has a new attribute id; Favorites that use the layer are not updated. Archicad keeps the shown, locked and wireframe state of a layer per open window: the new layer gets the old one's state in the current window and in every layer combination, and starts shown and unlocked in the other open windows. The model elements that sections, elevations, interior elevations and 3D documents show of the layer come back on the new layer when those views are rebuilt (listed as viewsToRebuild). dryRun lists the elements and tool defaults on each layer without changing anything. The whole call is one undo step. Available from Archicad 27.
Attribute Commands.method_code:
def reindex_layers(
    self,
    layers: list[Layer],
    dry_run: None | bool = None,
    max_placeholders: None | int = None
) -> list[ErrorItem | Layers]:
    """
    Moves layers to new indices. Archicad cannot renumber an attribute, so each layer is
    recreated at its new index (free indices below it are filled with temporary layers,
    which are deleted again), gets the old layer's state in every layer combination, and
    then every element of the old layer is moved to it, in the floor plan and in every view
    and layout database, with the tool defaults on that layer. Only when the old layer is
    empty everywhere is it deleted, and the new layer gets its name, flags and folder. If an
    element cannot be moved (it is locked, not reserved in Teamwork, or comes from a
    hotlinked module), that layer is left as it was. The new layer has a new attribute id;
    Favorites that use the layer are not updated. Archicad keeps the shown, locked and
    wireframe state of a layer per open window: the new layer gets the old one's state in
    the current window and in every layer combination, and starts shown and unlocked in the
    other open windows. The model elements that sections, elevations, interior elevations
    and 3D documents show of the layer come back on the new layer when those views are
    rebuilt (listed as viewsToRebuild). dryRun lists the elements and tool defaults on each
    layer without changing anything. The whole call is one undo step. Available from
    Archicad 27.

    Args:
        layers (list[Layer]): The layers to move to a new index, handled in the given order.
        dry_run (None | bool): Only list what would change (the elements on each layer, the
            tools whose default layer it is, the elements that block the move) without
            changing anything. The default is false.
        max_placeholders (None | int): Every free index below newIndex is filled with a
            temporary layer first (about 20 ms each), so a newIndex far above the highest
            index in use takes long. A layer that needs more temporary layers than this is
            not moved. The default is 1000.

    Returns:
        list[ErrorItem | Layers]: One item per requested layer, in the same order.

    Raises:
        ArchicadAPIError: If the API returns an error response.
        RequestError: If there is a network or connection error.
        pydantic.ValidationError: If the parameters, or the API Response fail validation.
    """
    params_dict = {
            'layers': layers,
            'dryRun': dry_run,
            'maxPlaceholders': max_placeholders,
        }
    validated_params = ReindexLayersParameters(**params_dict)
    response_dict = self._core.post_tapir_command(
        "ReindexLayers",
        validated_params.model_dump(mode='json', by_alias=True, exclude_none=True)
    )
    validated_response = ReindexLayersResult.model_validate(response_dict)
    return validated_response.layers

A and B are taken from the extent of the symbol. The elements themselves are not changed.
Library Commands.method_code:
def create_library_part_from_elements(
    self,
    name: str,
    elements: list[ElementIdArrayItem],
    parent_id: None | str = None,
    parent_name: None | str = None,
    folder: None | str = None,
    library_folder: None | str = None,
    overwrite: None | bool = None,
    placeable: None | bool = None,
    scripts: None | Scripts = None,
    comment: None | str = None,
    keywords: None | str = None
) -> CreateLibraryPartFromElementsResult:
    """
    Creates a library part in the embedded library (or in a given local library folder,
    which is added to the loaded libraries when needed) whose 2D symbol is a copy of the
    given 2D drawing elements (lines, polylines, arcs, circles, splines, fills, texts and
    hotspots), under the given parent subtype, with optional master, 2D, 3D and parameter
    scripts, comment and keywords. A and B are taken from the extent of the symbol. The
    elements themselves are not changed.

    Args:
        name (str): The name of the new library part, as shown in the library and used by
            CreateObjects as libraryPartName.
        elements (list[ElementIdArrayItem]): The 2D drawing elements (lines, polylines,
            arcs, circles, splines, fills, texts and hotspots) whose copies make up the 2D
            symbol of the new library part. They keep their plan coordinates, so the project
            origin becomes the origin of the symbol. The elements themselves are not
            changed.
        parent_id (None | str): The parent subtype of the new library part: its unique ID
            ('{main}-{revision}') or its main GUID, as GetAvailableLibraryParts reports it.
            Either parentId or parentName is required.
        parent_name (None | str): The document name of the parent subtype, e.g. 'General
            Object' or 'Model Element'; used when parentId is not given.
        folder (None | str): Optional. The folder of the new .gsm file, relative to the
            embedded library (or to libraryFolder), created when missing. By default the
            embedded library (or libraryFolder) itself.
        library_folder (None | str): Optional. The absolute path of a local library folder
            to create the library part in instead of the embedded library. A folder that is

def set_property_values_of_elements(
    self,
    element_property_values: list[ElementPropertyValueWithStatus | ElementPropertyValueWithValue]
) -> list[FailedExecutionResult | SuccessfulExecutionResult]:
    """
    Sets the property values of elements. It works for subelements of hierarchal elements
    also. With valueStatus an element's value can also be reset to the default value of the
    property (Default) or made undefined (UserUndefined, from 1.8.1). With dryRun true
    nothing is changed and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and
    each item that passes the checks made before writing gets wouldChange, with the
    element's value now (oldValue) and the value a real run would write (newValue), both as
    GetPropertyValuesOfElements gives them.

    Args:
        element_property_values (list[ElementPropertyValueWithStatus |
            ElementPropertyValueWithValue]): A single real value accepts '.' or ',' as the
            decimal separator, so the value strings GetPropertyValuesOfElements returns can
            be written back: when both appear the last one is the decimal separator, a
            separator that appears more than once groups thousands, and a single separator
            is the decimal one. Unitless real and integer lists accept semicolon-separated
            numbers; an empty string sets an empty list. Invalid items reject the entire
            property write.

    Returns:
        list[FailedExecutionResult | SuccessfulExecutionResult]: One result for each item of
            elementPropertyValues, in the order of the input. On a dry run an item that
            passes every check made before writing (the property values of the element can
            be read, the value is editable for the element and converts to the property's
            type) gets wouldChange: oldValue is the element's value now as
            GetPropertyValuesOfElements gives it (left out when the property is not
            available or not evaluated for the element), newValue the value that would be
            written in the same format (left out for valueStatus Default). Archicad can
            still refuse a value that passes them.

    Raises:
        ArchicadAPIError: If the API returns an error response.
        RequestError: If there is a network or connection error.
        pydantic.ValidationError: If the parameters, or the API Response fail validation.
    """
    params_dict = {
            'elementPropertyValues': element_property_values,
        }
    validated_params = SetPropertyValuesOfElementsParameters(**params_dict)
    response_dict = self._core.post_tapir_command(
        "SetPropertyValuesOfElements",
        validated_params.model_dump(mode='json', by_alias=True, exclude_none=True)
    )
    return TypeAdapter(list[ExecutionResult]).validate_python(response_dict.get('executionResults'))

Element Commands.name: DistributeElements
Element Commands.description: Distributes 3 or more elements on the floor plan or in the current 2D view evenly along X (horizontal) or Y (vertical), with equal distances between the middles of their plan bounding boxes (centers) or equal space between the boxes (gaps), by moving them in one undo step. The elements are taken in the order of their middles along the direction, and the two outermost stay where they are. The bounding boxes are those Get2DBoundingBoxes returns. Supported types: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Mesh, Zone, Object, Lamp, Stair, Railing, CurtainWall, Line, PolyLine, Arc, Circle, Spline, Hatch, Text and Hotspot. An element of another type (doors, windows and openings, which only slide along their host, subelements, dimensions, labels, ...) or one that cannot be edited gets a failed execution result naming the reason, and the other elements are still distributed.
Element Commands.method_code:
def distribute_elements(
    self,
    elements: list[ElementIdArrayItem],
    direction: Direction,
    mode: Mode
) -> list[FailedExecutionResult | SuccessfulExecutionResult]:
    """
    Distributes 3 or more elements on the floor plan or in the current 2D view evenly along
    X (horizontal) or Y (vertical), with equal distances between the middles of their plan
    bounding boxes (centers) or equal space between the boxes (gaps), by moving them in one
    undo step. The elements are taken in the order of their middles along the direction, and
    the two outermost stay where they are. The bounding boxes are those Get2DBoundingBoxes
    returns. Supported types: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Mesh, Zone,
    Object, Lamp, Stair, Railing, CurtainWall, Line, PolyLine, Arc, Circle, Spline, Hatch,
    Text and Hotspot. An element of another type (doors, windows and openings, which only
    slide along their host, subelements, dimensions, labels, ...) or one that cannot be
    edited gets a failed execution result naming the reason, and the other elements are
    still distributed.

    Args:
        elements (list[ElementIdArrayItem]): At least 3 elements to distribute: Wall,
            Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Mesh, Zone, Object, Lamp, Stair,
            Railing, CurtainWall, Line, PolyLine, Arc, Circle, Spline, Hatch, Text or
            Hotspot, in the current database. Their order does not matter: they are
            distributed in the order of the middles of their plan bounding boxes along the
            direction.

            Y. They are not moved in the other direction.
        mode (Mode): centers makes the distances between the middles of the plan bounding
            boxes equal, gaps makes the empty space between neighbouring bounding boxes
            equal (the gap is negative, so the boxes overlap, when the elements are wider
            together than the space between the two outermost elements).

            'direction': direction,

        "DistributeElements",
        validated_params.model_dump(mode='json', by_alias=True, exclude_none=True)
    )
    validated_response = DistributeElementsResult.model_validate(response_dict)
    return validated_response.executionResults

Element Commands.description: Gets the details of elements (geometry parameters etc). When elements is omitted, all elements matching the optional server-side filter (types, floorIndices, layerIndices) are queried; an empty elements list returns no details. Use the optional fields parameter to return only the fields you need (e.g. elementId, type, id, floorIndex) and skip the computation of the others (for example floorPlanPolygons). Use the optional additionalFields parameter to also get the info string, the compound info string, the library part unique ID and the creator tool unique ID. An element of another database (a layout, a section, a worksheet ...) returns only its header fields (type, floor index, layer, draw index) with fromOtherDatabase set to true.
Element Commands.method_code:
def get_details_of_elements(
    self,
    elements: None | list[ElementIdArrayItem] = None,
    fields: None | list[ElementDetailsField] = None,
    *,
    filter: ElementTypeFloorLayerFilter | None = None,
    additional_fields: None | list[ElementDetailsAdditionalField] = None
) -> list[DetailsOfElement | ElementHeaderFromOtherDatabase | ErrorItem]:
    """
    Gets the details of elements (geometry parameters etc). When elements is omitted, all
    elements matching the optional server-side filter (types, floorIndices, layerIndices)
    are queried; an empty elements list returns no details. Use the optional fields
    parameter to return only the fields you need (e.g. elementId, type, id, floorIndex) and
    skip the computation of the others (for example floorPlanPolygons). Use the optional
    additionalFields parameter to also get the info string, the compound info string, the
    library part unique ID and the creator tool unique ID. An element of another database (a
    layout, a section, a worksheet ...) returns only its header fields (type, floor index,
    layer, draw index) with fromOtherDatabase set to true.

    Args:
        elements (None | list[ElementIdArrayItem]): Optional list of elements to get details
            for. When omitted, all elements in the current database (optionally filtered by
            the filter parameter) are used; an empty list returns no details.
        fields (None | list[ElementDetailsField]): Optional filter for the fields to return
            for each element. When omitted, every field is returned. Fields not listed are
            not computed at all, so listing only what you need skips in particular the
            floorPlanPolygons extraction, which regenerates each element's 2D drawing
            primitives and can dominate the execution time of batch reads.
        filter (ElementTypeFloorLayerFilter | None): Optional server-side filter. Without
            elements, only the elements matching it are returned. A listed element that does
            not match it gets an error entry in its place.
        additional_fields (None | list[ElementDetailsAdditionalField]): Optional extra
            fields to return for each element, on top of the ones selected by fields. None
            of them is returned unless listed here, so callers that do not give this
            parameter get the same response as before.

    Returns:
        list[DetailsOfElement | ElementHeaderFromOtherDatabase | ErrorItem]: One entry per
            input element, in the same order as the input elements array. An element that
            cannot be read, or that does not match the filter, gets an error entry in its
            place, so the position of an entry tells which input element it belongs to.
            Without elements, one entry per element that matches the filter.

    Raises:
        ArchicadAPIError: If the API returns an error response.
        RequestError: If there is a network or connection error.
        pydantic.ValidationError: If the parameters, or the API Response fail validation.
    """
    params_dict = {
            'elements': elements,
            'fields': fields,
            'filter': filter,
            'additionalFields': additional_fields,
        }
    validated_params = GetDetailsOfElementsParameters(**params_dict)
    response_dict = self._core.post_tapir_command(
        "GetDetailsOfElements",
        validated_params.model_dump(mode='json', by_alias=True, exclude_none=True)
    )
    validated_response = GetDetailsOfElementsResult.model_validate(response_dict)
    return validated_response.detailsOfElements

Element Commands.name: SetElementNotificationClient
Element Commands.description: Sets up a new notification client to receive element events.
Element Commands.method_code:
def set_element_notification_client(
    self,
    port: int,
    host: None | str = None,
    notify_on_new_element: None | bool = None,
    notify_on_modification_of_an_element: None | bool = None,
    notify_on_reservation_changes: None | bool = None,
    *,
    element_types_to_observe: None | list[ElementType] = None,
    notify_on_selection_change: None | bool = None,
    notify_on_window_change: None | bool = None,
    notify_on_project_events: None | bool = None,
    notify_on_attribute_replacement: None | bool = None,
    notify_on_tool_change: None | bool = None,
    notify_on_view_events: None | bool = None,
    notify_on_lockable_reservation_changes: None | bool = None,
    notify_on_tool_default_changes: None | bool = None,
    notify_on_attribute_changes: None | bool = None,
    notify_on_classification_changes: None | bool = None,
    notify_on_property_definition_changes: None | bool = None,
    notify_on_marquee_change: None | bool = None,
    notify_on_3d_settings_changes: None | bool = None
) -> FailedExecutionResult | SuccessfulExecutionResult:
    """
    Sets up a new notification client to receive element events.

    Args:
        port (int): The port number of the notification client.
        host (None | str): The host address of the notification client. If not provided,
            localhost is used.
        notify_on_new_element (None | bool): Notify on creation of a new element. Optional
            parameter, by default true.
        notify_on_modification_of_an_element (None | bool): Notify on modification/deletion
            of an element. The observed elements are the ones ACAPI_Element_GetElemList
            returns, for API_ZombieElemID or, with elementTypesToObserve, for each of those
            types, when the first client asking for these notifications of them is
            registered, and every element of the observed types created after that. Archicad
            does not report the changes made by Tapir's own commands, so Tapir reports them
            itself for SetDetailsOfElements, SetPropertyValuesOfElements, MoveElements,
            RotateElements, MirrorElements (not for the copies they make, which are new
            elements), DeleteElements, DeleteSelectedElements, the Modify<Tool> commands
            (ModifyWalls, ModifyBeams, ModifySlabs, ModifyColumns, ModifyWindows,
            ModifyDoors, ModifyOpenings, ModifyMorphs, ModifyRoofs, ModifyShells,
            ModifyMeshes, ModifyObjects, ModifyLamps, ModifyTexts, ModifyLabels,
            ModifyCurtainWalls, ModifyCurtainWallFrames, ModifyZones, ModifySections,
            ModifyDetailMarkers, ModifyRailings, ModifyStairs), ChangeTextContent,
            SetGDLParametersOfElements, RunParameterScriptOfElements (only when the script
            changed the element), SetMarkerParametersOfElements,
            SetMarkerLibraryPartOfElements, ChangeLibraryPartOfElements,
            SetClassificationsOfElements, SetCategoryValuesOfElements,
            ModifyPropertyValueOfElements, SetElementInfoStrings,
            SetURLReferencesOfElements, SetIFCAttributesOfElements,
            SetIFCPropertiesOfElements, RemoveIFCPropertiesOfElements,
            SetIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements,
            RemoveIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements, LockElements, UnlockElements,
            SetOpeningDetails, SetOpeningFloorPlanParameters, SetOpeningSymbolParameters,
            CreateGroups and UngroupElements (the grouped elements),
            MoveElementsToDesignOptions, CreateSolidElementLinks, RemoveSolidElementLinks,
            CreateSolidOperations (the target and operator when the operation changed or
            deleted them; the results are new elements), TrimElements, RemoveElementTrims,
            MergeElements, UnmergeElements, ModifyMEPRoutingElements, ModifyMEPPorts (the
            element owning the port), ConnectMEPElements, ModifyMEPElements,
            SetMEPRoutingParameters, ModifyElectricalPanels, ModifyElectricalDevices and
            ConnectToElectricalCircuits. Of the elements these commands change, only the
            given ones are reported: an element deleted together with its owner (a door or
            window of a deleted wall) is not. UpdateZones is not reported by Tapir, because
            Archicad updates the Zones after the command has returned. When the user moves,
            rotates, mirrors, elevates, resizes or stretches elements in Archicad, each of
            their changedElements items also has a transformation: {"type": ..., ...}, where
            type is "Drag" (with displacement: {"x", "y", "z"}), "Elevate" (with
            displacement, only z is not 0), "Rotate" (with origin: {"x", "y"} and angle, in
            radians, counterclockwise), "Mirror" (with origin, a point of the mirror axis,
            and axisDirection: {"x", "y"}, its unit vector), "Resize" (with origin and
            ratio), "Stretch", "VerticalStretch", "PreservedHeightStretch",
            "PreservedDirectionStretch" or "General"; the changes made by Tapir's own
            commands and by undo or redo have no transformation. Optional parameter, by
            default true. Archicad attaches an observer to each element to observe (see
            elementTypesToObserve) when the first client asks for this, and detaches them
            when the last one stops, and it is blocked meanwhile: the time grows faster than
            the number of elements, from seconds for a few hundred elements to many minutes
            for a few thousand. Count the elements first (GetAllElements with
            IncludeSubElemObjects, or GetElementsByType) and limit the types on large
            projects.
        notify_on_reservation_changes (None | bool): Notify on reservation changes of an
            element. Optional parameter, by default true.
        element_types_to_observe (None | list[ElementType]): Only modifications/deletions of
            elements of these types are observed and notified to this client. Optional
            parameter, by default every element (including the parts of curtain walls,
            stairs and railings, which are most of the elements of large projects).
            Registering the same client again with other types changes them; only the
            elements of types no client observed before get an observer then. Does not limit
            the other notifications.
        notify_on_selection_change (None | bool): Notify when the selection changes. The
            message is {"selectedElements": [...]}: the whole current selection, each item
            an elementId as in the response of GetSelectedElements, an empty list when
            nothing is selected. Optional parameter, by default false.
        notify_on_window_change (None | bool): Notify when the current (active) window
            changes or the user switches to another story. The message is {"windowChanged":
            {"event": "Window" or "Floor", "windowType": ..., "databaseId": ...,
            "storyIndex": ...}}: windowType and databaseId describe the new current window
            as in the response of GetCurrentWindowType (databaseId is missing when that
            response has none), storyIndex is the active story, missing when it cannot be
            read. Optional parameter, by default false.
        notify_on_project_events (None | bool): Notify on project events. The message is
            {"projectEvent": ...}, one of "New", "NewAndReset", "Open", "Close", "Quit",
            "SendChanges" (a Teamwork send is about to start) and "ReceiveChanges" (Teamwork
            changes were received). The client stays registered when the project is closed
            or another one is opened. Optional parameter, by default false.
        notify_on_attribute_replacement (None | bool): Notify when attributes are deleted
            and replaced by other attributes of the same type (for example Delete and
            Replace in the Attribute Manager). The message is {"replacedAttributes":
            [{"attributeType": ..., "oldIndex": ..., "newIndex": ..., "newAttributeId":
            ...}, ...]}: attributeType is one of the type names of GetAttributesByType
            ("Layer", "Line", "Fill", "Composite", "Surface", "LayerCombination",
            "ZoneCategory", "Profile", "PenTable", "MEPSystem", "OperationProfile",
            "BuildingMaterial", or "Unknown"), oldIndex is the index of the replaced
            attribute and newIndex the index of the attribute that replaces it,
            newAttributeId is the attributeId of that attribute, missing when it cannot be
            found. Not available in Archicad 25: setting it to true there fails. Optional
            parameter, by default false.
        notify_on_tool_change (None | bool): Notify when the user switches to another tool
            in the Toolbox. The message is {"toolChanged": {"elementType": ...}}:
            elementType is the element type of the new tool, as in elementTypesToObserve
            (for example "Wall" or "Column"), "None" for the Arrow and the Marquee, and
            "Unknown" for a tool Tapir has no type name for. Optional parameter, by default
            false.
        notify_on_view_events (None | bool): Notify when an item of the Project Navigator or
            the Organizer is inserted (for example a view is saved or a layout is created),
            modified (for example renamed), deleted or opened. The message is {"viewEvent":
            {"event": ..., "navigatorMapId": ..., "navigatorItemId": {"guid": ...}}}: event
            is one of "Inserted", "Modified", "Deleted" and "Opened", navigatorMapId is the
            navigator map of the item, one of "ProjectMap", "PublicViewMap", "MyViewMap",
            "LayoutBook" and "PublisherSets" (as navigatorMapId of GetNavigatorItemTree),
            and navigatorItemId is the guid of the navigator item, as in the response of
            GetNavigatorItemTree (a deleted item no longer exists). Optional parameter, by
            default false.
        notify_on_lockable_reservation_changes (None | bool): Notify when a Teamwork
            lockable object set (the non-element things Teamwork reserves: the attributes of
            a type, favorites, model view options, project info, project preferences, ...)
            is reserved or released, by anyone, including the current user. The message is
            {"lockableReservationChanged": {"event": ..., "objectSetId": {"guid": ...},
            "objectSetName": ..., "reservedBy": ..., "reservedByUserId": ...}}: event is
            "Reserved" or "Released", objectSetId is the guid of the object set,
            objectSetName its name as objectSetName of ReserveLockableObjectSet (for example
            "Composites", "LayerSettingsDialog" or "Favorites"), missing when it is not one
            of the documented sets, and reservedBy and reservedByUserId are the name and the
            Teamwork user id of the member who reserved it, only for "Reserved". Element
            reservations are notified by notifyOnReservationChanges. Optional parameter, by
            default false.
        notify_on_tool_default_changes (None | bool): Notify when the default settings of a
            tool change (for example the user changes the settings of the Wall tool with no
            wall selected), so a client can read the new defaults. The message is
            {"toolDefaultsChanged": {"elementType": ...}}: elementType is the element type
            whose defaults changed, as in elementTypesToObserve (for example "Wall" or
            "Column"), and "Unknown" for a type Tapir has no type name for. Optional
            parameter, by default false.
        notify_on_attribute_changes (None | bool): Notify when attributes (layers, fills,
            composites, surfaces, building materials, ...) are created, modified or deleted.
            The message is {"attributesChanged": {"event": ..., "attributeIds":
            [{"attributeId": {"guid": ...}}, ...]}}: event is "Created", "Modified" or
            "Deleted", and attributeIds are the attributes, as in the response of
            GetAttributesByType (a deleted attribute no longer exists). Not available in
            Archicad 25: setting it to true there fails. Optional parameter, by default
            false.
        notify_on_classification_changes (None | bool): Notify when classification systems
            or classification items are created, modified or deleted. The messages are
            {"classificationSystemsChanged": {"event": ..., "classificationSystemIds":
            [{"classificationSystemId": {"guid": ...}}, ...]}} and
            {"classificationItemsChanged": {"event": ..., "classificationItemIds":
            [{"classificationItemId": {"guid": ...}}, ...]}}: event is "Created", "Modified"
            or "Deleted", and the ids are as in the response of GetAllClassificationSystems
            and GetAllClassificationsInSystem. Not available in Archicad 25: setting it to
            true there fails. Optional parameter, by default false.
        notify_on_property_definition_changes (None | bool): Notify when property groups or
            property definitions are created, modified or deleted (property values of
            elements are notified as changedElements by notifyOnModificationOfAnElement).
            The messages are {"propertyGroupsChanged": {"event": ..., "propertyGroupIds":
            [{"propertyGroupId": {"guid": ...}}, ...]}} and {"propertyDefinitionsChanged":
            {"event": ..., "propertyIds": [{"propertyId": {"guid": ...}}, ...]}}: event is
            "Created", "Modified" or "Deleted", and the ids are as in the response of
            GetAllProperties. Not available in Archicad 25: setting it to true there fails.
            Optional parameter, by default false.
        notify_on_marquee_change (None | bool): Notify when the marquee is drawn, changed or
            removed. The message is {"marqueeChanged": {"type": ..., "multiStory": ...}}:
            type is "rectangle", "rotatedRectangle", "polygon" or, when the marquee was
            removed, "none", as type of GetMarquee, which returns the shape of the marquee;
            multiStory is missing for "none". Available from Archicad 27: setting it to true
            in an earlier version fails. Optional parameter, by default false.
        notify_on_3d_settings_changes (None | bool): Notify when the settings of the 3D
            window change (projection, Filter and Cut Elements in 3D, 3D window settings).
            The message is {"view3DSettingsChanged": {}}; read the new settings with the
            commands of the 3D window. The changes made while navigating in 3D are not
            notified. Available from Archicad 30: setting it to true in an earlier version
            fails. Optional parameter, by default false.

    Returns:
        FailedExecutionResult | SuccessfulExecutionResult

    Raises:
        ArchicadAPIError: If the API returns an error response.
        RequestError: If there is a network or connection error.
        pydantic.ValidationError: If the parameters, or the API Response fail validation.
    """
    params_dict = {
            'host': host,
            'port': port,
            'notifyOnNewElement': notify_on_new_element,
            'notifyOnModificationOfAnElement': notify_on_modification_of_an_element,
            'elementTypesToObserve': element_types_to_observe,
            'notifyOnReservationChanges': notify_on_reservation_changes,
            'notifyOnSelectionChange': notify_on_selection_change,
            'notifyOnWindowChange': notify_on_window_change,
            'notifyOnProjectEvents': notify_on_project_events,
            'notifyOnAttributeReplacement': notify_on_attribute_replacement,
            'notifyOnToolChange': notify_on_tool_change,
            'notifyOnViewEvents': notify_on_view_events,
            'notifyOnLockableReservationChanges': notify_on_lockable_reservation_changes,
            'notifyOnToolDefaultChanges': notify_on_tool_default_changes,
            'notifyOnAttributeChanges': notify_on_attribute_changes,
            'notifyOnClassificationChanges': notify_on_classification_changes,
            'notifyOnPropertyDefinitionChanges': notify_on_property_definition_changes,
            'notifyOnMarqueeChange': notify_on_marquee_change,
            'notifyOn3DSettingsChanges': notify_on_3d_settings_changes,
        }
    validated_params = SetElementNotificationClientParameters(**params_dict)
    response_dict = self._core.post_tapir_command(
        "SetElementNotificationClient",
        validated_params.model_dump(mode='json', by_alias=True, exclude_none=True)
    )
    validated_response = TypeAdapter(SetElementNotificationClientResult).validate_python(response_dict)
    return validated_response

Element Commands.name: SetGDLParametersOfElements
Element Commands.description: Sets the given GDL parameters of the given elements. An element Archicad does not let the user edit (its layer locked, the element locked, or not reserved by the user in Teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming that reason, whatever the parameter. On a Curtain Wall Frame, A, B, ac_frameWidth and ac_frameDepth mirror the frame's contour, which Archicad derives from the frame's settings, so they are rejected instead of reporting a change that does not take effect; a frame without a library part (an invisible Boundary frame, for example) has no GDL parameters. The parameters are read back after the change, and a written parameter Archicad did not keep (e.g. one it sets from the element's own settings, like AC_TextSize_1 of a label) gives a failed execution result naming it. With dryRun true no element is changed and no undo step is created: the parameters are written to the element's parameter list and its Parameter Script runs as in a real run, the response has dryRun set to true, and each element that passes the checks made before changing it gets wouldChange, listing the parameters a real run would change (the given ones and the ones the Parameter Script changes with them) with their old and new values.

def set_gdl_parameters_of_elements(
    self,
    elements_with_gdl_parameters: list[ElementsWithGDLParameter]
) -> list[FailedExecutionResult | SuccessfulExecutionResult]:
    """
    Sets the given GDL parameters of the given elements. An element Archicad does not let
    the user edit (its layer locked, the element locked, or not reserved by the user in
    Teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming that reason, whatever the parameter. On
    a Curtain Wall Frame, A, B, ac_frameWidth and ac_frameDepth mirror the frame's contour,
    which Archicad derives from the frame's settings, so they are rejected instead of
    reporting a change that does not take effect; a frame without a library part (an
    invisible Boundary frame, for example) has no GDL parameters. The parameters are read
    back after the change, and a written parameter Archicad did not keep (e.g. one it sets
    from the element's own settings, like AC_TextSize_1 of a label) gives a failed execution
    result naming it. With dryRun true no element is changed and no undo step is created:
    the parameters are written to the element's parameter list and its Parameter Script runs
    as in a real run, the response has dryRun set to true, and each element that passes the
    checks made before changing it gets wouldChange, listing the parameters a real run would
    change (the given ones and the ones the Parameter Script changes with them) with their
    old and new values.

    Args:
        elements_with_gdl_parameters (list[ElementsWithGDLParameter]): The elements with GDL
            parameters dictionary pairs.

    Returns:
        list[FailedExecutionResult | SuccessfulExecutionResult]: One result for each item of
            elementsWithGDLParameters, in the order of the input. On a dry run the
            parameters are written to the element's parameter list and its Parameter Script
            runs as in a real run, but the element is not changed. An element that passes
            every check made before changing it (the element and its parameters exist, every
            value is valid for its parameter, the element is editable) gets wouldChange:
            oldValue and newValue list the parameters a real run would change - the ones
            given and the ones the Parameter Script changes with them - before and after,
            each with name, index, type and value as GetGDLParametersOfElements gives them.
            Archicad can still refuse an element that passes them.

    Raises:
        ArchicadAPIError: If the API returns an error response.
        RequestError: If there is a network or connection error.
        pydantic.ValidationError: If the parameters, or the API Response fail validation.
    """

            'elementsWithGDLParameters': elements_with_gdl_parameters,
        }
    validated_params = SetGDLParametersOfElementsParameters(**params_dict)
    response_dict = self._core.post_tapir_command(
        "SetGDLParametersOfElements",
        validated_params.model_dump(mode='json', by_alias=True, exclude_none=True)
    )
    return TypeAdapter(list[ExecutionResult]).validate_python(response_dict.get('executionResults'))

Element Commands.name: SplitElements
Element Commands.description: Splits each given element along a line (the infinite line through its begin and end point, like Archicad's Split command). The original element keeps one part, copies of it (Drag a Copy, so they keep the layer, classifications, properties and every other setting) get the others; all are returned, the original first. Supports straight walls without doors, windows or openings, straight unslanted single segment beams without holes or openings, and lines (their arrows stay at the original ends), which are split in two, the original keeping the part from its begin point; and slabs, meshes without level lines or points, fills and single contour polylines, whose polygon (holes and arcs included) or points are cut along the line into one part per piece, the original keeping the largest piece (a polyline: the piece with its begin point). Slab edges keep their trim and side surface, the edges along the line are vertical; the corners a mesh gets on the line take their height from the edge they lie on. An element the line does not cross is reported as notCut, an unsupported one as an error naming its type. One undo step.
Element Commands.method_code:
def split_elements(
    self,
    elements: list[ElementIdArrayItem],
    line: Line
) -> list[ElementNotSplit | ErrorItem | SplitElementParts]:
    """
    Splits each given element along a line (the infinite line through its begin and end
    point, like Archicad's Split command). The original element keeps one part, copies of it
    (Drag a Copy, so they keep the layer, classifications, properties and every other
    setting) get the others; all are returned, the original first. Supports straight walls
    without doors, windows or openings, straight unslanted single segment beams without
    holes or openings, and lines (their arrows stay at the original ends), which are split
    in two, the original keeping the part from its begin point; and slabs, meshes without
    level lines or points, fills and single contour polylines, whose polygon (holes and arcs
    included) or points are cut along the line into one part per piece, the original keeping
    the largest piece (a polyline: the piece with its begin point). Slab edges keep their
    trim and side surface, the edges along the line are vertical; the corners a mesh gets on
    the line take their height from the edge they lie on. An element the line does not cross
    is reported as notCut, an unsupported one as an error naming its type. One undo step.

    Args:
        elements (list[ElementIdArrayItem]): The elements to split. Supported: straight
            walls (not polygonal, without doors, windows or openings), straight beams (not
            slanted or curved, one segment, without holes or openings), lines, slabs, meshes
            (without level lines or points), fills and polylines (one contour). Other types

        line (Line): The split line in project coordinates: the infinite line through begin

    Returns:

def update_zones(
    self,
    keep_stamp_position: None | bool = None,
    undo_top_trim: None | bool = None,
    undo_bottom_trim: None | bool = None,
    *,
    zones: None | list[ElementIdArrayItem] = None
) -> FailedExecutionResult | SuccessfulExecutionResult:
    """
    Updates Zones (recalculates their geometry, updates their Zone Stamps and the connected
    elements): the selected Zones, every Zone when nothing is selected, or the Zones given
    in zones. Archicad runs the update right after the command has returned, on the Zones
    selected at that moment, so the new geometry can only be read with a later command.

    Args:
        keep_stamp_position (None | bool): Keep the position of the Zone Stamps. The default
            is true.
        undo_top_trim (None | bool): Undo the trimming of the top of the Zones. The default
            is false.
        undo_bottom_trim (None | bool): Undo the trimming of the bottom of the Zones. The
            default is false.
        zones (None | list[ElementIdArrayItem]): Optional list of the Zones to update, on
            any story. They are selected instead of the current selection and stay selected:
            Archicad updates the selected Zones right after the command has returned, not
            during it, and clears the selection when it is done. So do not change the
            selection until then, and read the new geometry with a later command. Every Zone
            is checked first; if one cannot be updated (not a Zone, listed twice, hidden or
            locked layer, not editable), nothing is selected or updated. An empty list
            updates nothing. Without the list the current selection is updated, or every
            Zone when nothing is selected.

Favorites Commands.name: ApplyFavoritesToElements
Favorites Commands.description: Apply the given favorites to existing elements. Only settings-type parameters are changed - geometry (position, floor, and dimensions such as a Wall's height) is left untouched, so applying a Favorite never moves the target element. A Window or Door keeps its wall, marker and placement, and takes the Favorite's library part and parameters, size included. For the hierarchical types (Stair, Railing, Curtain Wall) the settings of the sub-elements are not applied, because they are inseparable from the Favorite's own geometry. By default settings, classifications, categories and properties are all applied; each can be opted out of individually. keepFields lists fields of the target (its ID, layer, an opening's width, height and sill height, a Wall's reference line location, height and top link) that are copied back after the Favorite has been applied, so that e.g. only the library part or the wall type changes. With favorite instead of favoritesToApply, one Favorite is read once and applied to the given elements, or to every element of its type that matches the filter.
Favorites Commands.method_code:
def apply_favorites_to_elements(
    self,
    favorites_to_apply: None | list[FavoriteToApply] = None,
    apply_settings: None | bool = None,
    apply_classifications: None | bool = None,
    apply_categories: None | bool = None,
    apply_properties: None | bool = None,
    keep_fields: None | list[FavoriteKeepField] = None,
    *,
    favorite: None | str = None,
    elements: None | list[ElementIdArrayItem] = None,
    filter: ElementTypeFloorLayerFilter | None = None
) -> list[FailedExecutionResult | SuccessfulExecutionResult]:
    """
    Apply the given favorites to existing elements. Only settings-type parameters are
    changed - geometry (position, floor, and dimensions such as a Wall's height) is left
    untouched, so applying a Favorite never moves the target element. A Window or Door keeps
    its wall, marker and placement, and takes the Favorite's library part and parameters,
    size included. For the hierarchical types (Stair, Railing, Curtain Wall) the settings of
    the sub-elements are not applied, because they are inseparable from the Favorite's own
    geometry. By default settings, classifications, categories and properties are all
    applied; each can be opted out of individually. keepFields lists fields of the target
    (its ID, layer, an opening's width, height and sill height, a Wall's reference line
    location, height and top link) that are copied back after the Favorite has been applied,
    so that e.g. only the library part or the wall type changes. With favorite instead of
    favoritesToApply, one Favorite is read once and applied to the given elements, or to
    every element of its type that matches the filter.

    Args:
        favorites_to_apply (None | list[FavoriteToApply]): The elements and the Favorite to
            apply to each. Give this or favorite.
        apply_settings (None | bool): Whether to apply the Favorite's settings-type
            parameters (structure, materials, pens, etc.). Geometry (position, floor, and
            dimensions such as a Wall's height) is never applied - the element stays on its
            own home story - except that a Window or Door takes the Favorite's library part
            and parameters, size included, while keeping its wall, marker and placement. For
            the hierarchical types (Stair, Railing, Curtain Wall) the settings of the sub-
            elements are not applied, because they are inseparable from the Favorite's own
            geometry. A Dimension's text size, text pen and text frame are not changed
            (tested in Archicad 28): the dimension creation commands take textHeight,
            textPen and textFrame for them. Default is true.
        apply_classifications (None | bool): Whether to apply the Favorite's
            classifications. Default is true.
        apply_categories (None | bool): Whether to apply the Favorite's element categories
            (e.g. IFC categories). Default is true.
        apply_properties (None | bool): Whether to apply the Favorite's property values.
            Default is true.
        keep_fields (None | list[FavoriteKeepField]): Fields of the target element to keep:
            after the Favorite has been applied, they are copied back from the target as it
            was before, so only the Favorite's other settings (e.g. its library part or wall
            type) take effect. 'id' and 'layerIndex' apply to every element type; 'width',
            'height' and 'sillHeight' to a Window or Door ('width' and 'height' also to a
            Skylight); 'height', 'topOffset' and 'relativeTopStory' to a Wall or Column;
            'referenceLineLocation' to a Wall. A field the target's type does not have is
            ignored. To keep a Wall's or Column's top exactly as it was, keep 'height',
            'relativeTopStory' and 'topOffset' together - a kept 'height' alone is
            recomputed by Archicad while the Favorite's relativeTopStory links the top to a
            story. Default: nothing is kept.
        favorite (None | str): The name of one Favorite to apply to many elements, instead
            of favoritesToApply: to the given elements, or without elements to every element
            of the Favorite's type that matches the filter. The Favorite is read only once.
            Needs elements or filter.
        elements (None | list[ElementIdArrayItem]): The elements to apply the single
            favorite to, one execution result each, in the same order. Only with favorite.
        filter (ElementTypeFloorLayerFilter | None): Server-side element filter for the
            single favorite. Without elements the favorite is applied to every element of
            its type that matches it; an element of elements that does not match it gets a
            failed execution result. Only with favorite.

    Returns:
        list[FailedExecutionResult | SuccessfulExecutionResult]: A list of execution
            results.

    Raises:
        ArchicadAPIError: If the API returns an error response.
        RequestError: If there is a network or connection error.
        pydantic.ValidationError: If the parameters, or the API Response fail validation.
    """
    params_dict = {
            'favoritesToApply': favorites_to_apply,
            'favorite': favorite,
            'elements': elements,
            'filter': filter,
            'applySettings': apply_settings,
            'applyClassifications': apply_classifications,
            'applyCategories': apply_categories,
            'applyProperties': apply_properties,
            'keepFields': keep_fields,
        }
    validated_params = ApplyFavoritesToElementsParameters(**params_dict)
    response_dict = self._core.post_tapir_command(
        "ApplyFavoritesToElements",
        validated_params.model_dump(mode='json', by_alias=True, exclude_none=True)
    )
    validated_response = ApplyFavoritesToElementsResult.model_validate(response_dict)
    return validated_response.executionResults

def export_favorites(
    self,
    path: str,
    names: None | list[str] = None,
    format: FavoriteExportFormat | None = None,
    *,
    overwrite: None | bool = None
) -> FailedExecutionResult | SuccessfulExecutionResult:
    """
    Export the project's Favorites to a .prefs file or folder. From Archicad 29 they can
    also be exported to a folder of Favorite files (xml format) or to a legacy .prf file
    (legacyPRF format). With overwrite false an export to a single file refuses to replace
    an existing file.

            matches the Favorite binary format (.prefs), writes a single file; otherwise

            Archicad 29 or newer.

            false refuses to export when a file already exists at path, and writes nothing.
            It needs an export to a single file (prefs format with a .prefs path, or
            legacyPRF format); with an export to a folder it is an error, as the names of
            the files written there are Archicad's.

    they can also be imported from a folder of Favorite files (xml format, all of them or

Project Commands.method_code:
def photo_render(
    self,
    image_file_path: str,
    format: None | PhotoRenderFormat = None,
    scene_name: None | str = None,
    *,
    overwrite: None | bool = None,
    width: None | int = None,
    height: None | int = None,
    resolution: None | int = None
) -> FailedExecutionResult | SuccessfulExecutionResult:
    """
    Renders the 3D model with the current rendering scene, or with the given one, as
    Document > Creative Imaging > PhotoRender Projection does, and saves the image to a file
    (png, jpg, bmp, tiff or gif). The image size, resolution and quality come from the
    scene; a width, height or resolution given here is used for this render only, the scene
    is not changed. With overwrite false it refuses to replace an existing file.

    Args:
        image_file_path (str): Absolute path of the image file to write. An existing file is
            overwritten, unless overwrite is false.
        format (None | PhotoRenderFormat)
        scene_name (None | str): Optional. The rendering scene to render with, one of the
            names GetRenderingScenes returns. It is made the current scene first, as
            SetCurrentRenderingScene does, and stays current afterwards. Omitted, the
            current scene is used.
        overwrite (None | bool): Optional, true by default. false refuses to render when a
            file already exists at imageFilePath, and writes nothing.
        width (None | int): Optional. The width of the image in pixels (the Size field of
            the PhotoRendering Settings palette). Omitted, the width of the scene is used.
            The image settings of the scene are changed for this render only and restored
            afterwards.
        height (None | int): Optional. The height of the image in pixels (the Size field of
            the PhotoRendering Settings palette). Omitted, the height of the scene is used.
            The image settings of the scene are changed for this render only and restored
            afterwards.
        resolution (None | int): Optional. The resolution of the image in dpi (the
            Resolution field of the PhotoRendering Settings palette). Omitted, the
            resolution of the scene is used. The image settings of the scene are changed for
            this render only and restored afterwards.

    Returns:
        FailedExecutionResult | SuccessfulExecutionResult

    Raises:
        ArchicadAPIError: If the API returns an error response.
        RequestError: If there is a network or connection error.
        pydantic.ValidationError: If the parameters, or the API Response fail validation.
    """
    params_dict = {
            'imageFilePath': image_file_path,
            'overwrite': overwrite,
            'format': format,
            'sceneName': scene_name,
            'width': width,
            'height': height,
            'resolution': resolution,
        }
    validated_params = PhotoRenderParameters(**params_dict)
    response_dict = self._core.post_tapir_command(
        "PhotoRender",
        validated_params.model_dump(mode='json', by_alias=True, exclude_none=True)
    )

Project Commands.name: ResolveNames
Project Commands.description: Looks up words or phrases (for example from a user's question) among the names of the open project before they are passed to other commands: stories, layers, layer combinations, building materials, composites, profiles, surfaces, fills, lines, zone categories, element types (by API name and, from Archicad 27, by the name the Archicad interface shows), properties (by name, and by group and name together) and classifications (systems by name and version, items of every system by name and ID). For each name it returns 'found' with the items named exactly so, 'closeMatches' with the nearest names, best first (ranked by differences in case, accents, spacing and separators, shared words, one name containing the other and a few differing characters), or 'notFound' when nothing in the project is close, meaning the project has no such item and it must not be guessed. Each match carries what the other commands take: the story index, the attribute id and index, the elementType, the propertyId (with the property's group, value type and the classification items a custom property is available for), or the classificationSystemId and classificationItemId. Matching is lexical and deterministic. Read only.
Project Commands.method_code:
def resolve_names(
    self,
    names: list[NameToResolve],
    max_close_matches: None | int = None
) -> list[ResolvedName]:
    """
    Looks up words or phrases (for example from a user's question) among the names of the
    open project before they are passed to other commands: stories, layers, layer
    combinations, building materials, composites, profiles, surfaces, fills, lines, zone
    categories, element types (by API name and, from Archicad 27, by the name the Archicad
    interface shows), properties (by name, and by group and name together) and
    classifications (systems by name and version, items of every system by name and ID). For
    each name it returns 'found' with the items named exactly so, 'closeMatches' with the
    nearest names, best first (ranked by differences in case, accents, spacing and
    separators, shared words, one name containing the other and a few differing characters),
    or 'notFound' when nothing in the project is close, meaning the project has no such item
    and it must not be guessed. Each match carries what the other commands take: the story
    index, the attribute id and index, the elementType, the propertyId (with the property's
    group, value type and the classification items a custom property is available for), or
    the classificationSystemId and classificationItemId. Matching is lexical and
    deterministic. Read only.

    Args:
        names (list[NameToResolve]): The words or phrases to look up in the open project,
            for example taken from a user's question.
        max_close_matches (None | int): The most close matches returned for one word, best
            first. The default is 5.

    Returns:
        list[ResolvedName]: One result for each of the given names, in the same order.

    Raises:
        ArchicadAPIError: If the API returns an error response.
        RequestError: If there is a network or connection error.
        pydantic.ValidationError: If the parameters, or the API Response fail validation.
    """
    params_dict = {
            'names': names,
            'maxCloseMatches': max_close_matches,
        }
    validated_params = ResolveNamesParameters(**params_dict)
    response_dict = self._core.post_tapir_command(
        "ResolveNames",
        validated_params.model_dump(mode='json', by_alias=True, exclude_none=True)
    )
    validated_response = ResolveNamesResult.model_validate(response_dict)
    return validated_response.results

Solid Element Operation Commands.description: Trims construction elements with a roof or shell: the roofs and shells in the list, or one given trimming element with a trim type. Solid Element Operation Commands.method_code:
def trim_elements(
    self,
    elements: list[ElementIdArrayItem],
    trimming_element: ElementId | None = None,
    trim_type: None | TrimType = None
) -> FailedExecutionResult | SuccessfulExecutionResult:
    """
    Trims construction elements with a roof or shell: the roofs and shells in the list, or
    one given trimming element with a trim type. With several roofs or shells in the list
    Archicad decides which of them trims which element (they may also trim each other), so
    not every element is necessarily trimmed by each; to trim each element with each roof or
    shell, call it once per roof or shell with trimmingElement, and check the result with
    GetElementTrims.

    Args:
        elements (list[ElementIdArrayItem]): The construction elements to trim. Without
            trimmingElement the roofs and shells among them do the trimming: Archicad
            decides which roof or shell trims which element and with which trim type, and
            may trim the roofs and shells with each other, so not every element is
            necessarily trimmed by every roof or shell. The call reports no result per pair;
            read them back with GetElementTrims. For a known result, use trimmingElement and
            call the command once per roof or shell.
        trimming_element (ElementId | None): Optional. The roof or shell that trims every
            element in the list, with trimType.
        trim_type (None | TrimType): Used with trimmingElement; defaults to KeepInside.

    Returns:
        FailedExecutionResult | SuccessfulExecutionResult

    Raises:
        ArchicadAPIError: If the API returns an error response.
        RequestError: If there is a network or connection error.
        pydantic.ValidationError: If the parameters, or the API Response fail validation.
    """
    params_dict = {
            'elements': elements,
            'trimmingElement': trimming_element,
            'trimType': trim_type,

IFC Commands.name: IFCFileOperation
IFC Commands.description: Executes an IFC file operation: opens or merges an IFC file, or saves the project as an IFC file. A save can name the export translator to use, a merge the story the IFC file's first storey is placed on. With overwrite false a save refuses to replace an existing file.
IFC Commands.method_code:
def ifc_file_operation(
    self,
    method: Method,
    ifc_file_path: str,
    file_type: FileType | None = None,
    translator_name: None | str = None,
    elements_to_export: IFCElementsToExport | None = None,
    *,
    overwrite: None | bool = None,
    story_index: None | int = None
) -> FailedExecutionResult | SuccessfulExecutionResult:
    """
    Executes an IFC file operation: opens or merges an IFC file, or saves the project as an
    IFC file. A save can name the export translator to use, a merge the story the IFC file's
    first storey is placed on. With overwrite false a save refuses to replace an existing
    file.

    Args:
        method (Method): The file operation method to use.
        ifc_file_path (str): The target IFC file to use. The save method overwrites an
            existing file, unless overwrite is false.
        file_type (FileType | None): The type of the IFC file. The default is 'ifc'.
        translator_name (None | str): Only for the save method: the name of the IFC export
            translator to save with, as GetIFCExportTranslators lists them. Without it the
            save runs with the translator Archicad would offer in its own Save dialog. Needs
            a fileType of ifc or ifczip (ifc or ifcxml on Archicad 25 and 26).
        elements_to_export (IFCElementsToExport | None): Only for the save method, and only
            together with translatorName. The default is VisibleElementsOnAllStories.
        overwrite (None | bool): Optional, true by default. Only for the save method: false
            refuses to save when a file already exists at ifcFilePath, and writes nothing.
        story_index (None | int): Only for the merge method: the story the first storey of
            the IFC file is placed on, the IFC's other storeys follow on the stories above
            it. Without it Archicad uses the active story of the floor plan. The active
            story and the current window are restored after the merge. See GetStories for
            the valid story indices.

    Returns:
        FailedExecutionResult | SuccessfulExecutionResult

    Raises:
        ArchicadAPIError: If the API returns an error response.
        RequestError: If there is a network or connection error.
        pydantic.ValidationError: If the parameters, or the API Response fail validation.
    """
    params_dict = {
            'method': method,
            'ifcFilePath': ifc_file_path,
            'overwrite': overwrite,
            'fileType': file_type,
            'translatorName': translator_name,
            'elementsToExport': elements_to_export,
            'storyIndex': story_index,
        }
    validated_params = IFCFileOperationParameters(**params_dict)
    response_dict = self._core.post_tapir_command(
        "IFCFileOperation",
        validated_params.model_dump(mode='json', by_alias=True, exclude_none=True)
    )
    validated_response = TypeAdapter(IFCFileOperationResult).validate_python(response_dict)
    return validated_response

def rename_navigator_item(
    self,
    navigator_item_id: NavigatorItemId,
    new_name: str | None = None,
    new_id: str | None = None
) -> None:
    """
    Renames an existing navigator item by specifying either the name or the ID, or both.

    Args:
        navigator_item_id (NavigatorItemId): The identifier of the navigator item to rename.
        new_name (str, optional): The new name for the navigator item.
        new_id (str, optional): The new ID for the navigator item.

    Raises:
        ArchicadAPIError: If the API returns an error response.
        RequestError: If there is a network or connection error.
        pydantic.ValidationError: If the parameters, or the API Response fail validation.
    """
    if not new_name and not new_id:
        raise ValueError("Either 'new_name' or 'new_id' (or both) must be provided.")

    if new_name and new_id:
        inner_model = RenameNavigatorItemByNameAndId(navigatorItemId=navigator_item_id, newName=new_name, newId=new_id)
    elif new_name:
        inner_model = RenameNavigatorItemByName(navigatorItemId=navigator_item_id, newName=new_name)
    else:
        inner_model = RenameNavigatorItemById(navigatorItemId=navigator_item_id, newId=new_id)

    validated_params = RenameNavigatorItemParameters(root=inner_model)
    self._core.post_command(
        "API.RenameNavigatorItem", validated_params.model_dump(mode='json', by_alias=True, exclude_none=True)
    )
    return None
